messages:
alex: Hey all — PR up: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/redispatcher/pull/482
alex: TL;DR: adds a lightweight redispatcher to reduce head-of-line blocking when KV prefetch bursts fill pinned allocation slots. Should shrink tail latency spikes under heavy mixed workloads.
alex: What I need: runtime eyes on hot-path latency tradeoffs, infra eyes on allocator/gating changes, security eyes on KMS/HSM usage. Hoping to merge early next week if we can get sign-offs. Can y'all take a look? @mike @jin @sarah :wave:

mike: I can take runtime. Quick ask: can you paste 95/99/99.9 pct numbers from the staging perf runs? Need before I kick off kernel-specific perf tests. Also, did you try this with quantized kernels?

alex: pasted numbers below from the staging run (staging cluster v3):
```
baseline (no redispatch): 95: 12ms  99: 48ms  99.9: 220ms
with redispatcher (same load): 95: 13ms  99: 99ms  99.9: 130ms
notes: tail (99.9) improved ~40%, 99 improved ~50% relative to baseline in mixed read/write at 8k qps
```
alex: quantized kernels: not yet — ran fp16 and int8 emulation on CPU. Will schedule a quantized GPU run if runtime wants it.

mike: OK that 99.9 drop looks promising. Please add a short perf script/instructions I can run (+ Docker image tag) so I can reproduce locally. Once I can repro I'll run kernel-specific tests. :+1:

jin: I can own infra review. Couple questions: does allocator change require rolling eviction of pinned slots? If so we need a rollout gate and a small canary window. Also pls add a feature flag (ops toggle) so we can disable redispatcher without a full rollback.

alex: Good call — added a canary flag in the PR (flag: redispatcher.enabled) and included an ops runbook link in the description: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ops/redispatcher-canary. Runbook includes rollback commands and simple health checks.

alex: For allocator: change is additive, it only modifies dispatch ordering; it does not evict pinned allocations proactively. I'll add explicit callouts in the PR and the rollout doc.

jin: Cool. I will request the gate: canary at 0.5% for 2 hours, then 5% for 4h, then 100% if no regressions. Assigning myself as canary owner for the first two steps.

sarah: Security: quick question — you mentioned KMS/HSM for key wrapping in the PR. Are any keys ever exported or persisted outside our HSM? Also need a short threat-model blurb and a sample test vector for replay/injection tests.

alex: No exports — keys used solely for envelope encryption inside the HSM path, never persisted as plaintext. I'll add the threat-model section (3 bullet points) and attach a sample test vector JSON in the PR by EOD.

mike: Once you add the perf script and quant runs, ping me and I'll schedule kernel runs tomorrow morning (UTC). If results look ok I'll sign off on runtime.

sarah: I'll do a quick security pass once the threat model + test vector are in. Expecting to post comments by EOD today.

deploy-bot: staging perf job queued: redispatcher/staging/perf-2025-03-02-09-00 UTC — job id 98821

alex: Thanks everyone — I'll update the PR with the perf script, quant run results, threat model, and ops gating plan. Hoping to merge Tuesday morning if all good. :rocket:

mike: Sounds good. If anyone else who cares (observability or SRE) wants to peek, pls add them; I can only cover hot-path perf.

jin: I'll add the rollout gates to the PR and the canary checklist. Will post the canary schedule in #eng-sre after merge.

sarah: ack, will follow up. :lock:

alex: pinging again — PR now has perf script + sample quant run logs + threat-model blurb. @mike @jin @sarah — friendly bump for final thumbs.
